Dear featureCounts team,

I am using featureCounts for getting read counts. I want to get gene, transcript and exon level read counts for rnaseq data.
Prior to featureCounts I used star for alignment.

For getting gene level readcounts I am using the below command:

featureCounts -p -t exon -s 0 -T 12 -g gene_id -a genes.gtf -o featurecounts.txt sample.starAligned.sortedByCoord.out.bam

Can i use -g option as "transcript_id" to get transcript level read counts?

And I want to perform exon level read counts. What options do I need to provide to get exon level counts?

Could you please help me.

Thanks In Advance
Fazulur Rehaman

messages.subject: Re: getting exon and transcript based read counts using featureCounts
messages.subject_clean: getting exon and transcript based read counts using featureCounts
messages.body_plain:
Dear Fazulur Rehaman,

You can use "-g transcript_id" to count reads to transcripts. But the difficulty lies in the counting of those reads that overlap more than one transcript and the number of such reads could be quite substantial. featureCounts provides several options for counting multi-overlapping reads, such as fractional counting. However you may try other transcript quantification tools as well, such as Kallisto and Salmon.

Regarding exon level counting, you will need to count at the feature level instead of meta-feature level. You can use the following command to get exon level counts:

featureCounts -p -t exon -s 0 -T 12 -f -O -a genes.gtf -o featurecounts.txt sample.starAligned.sortedByCoord.out.bam

'-f' option specifies feature level counting and '-O' allow reads overlapping more than one exon to be counted to all overlapping exons.

Best wishes,

Wei

messages.body_plain:
If you suspect that the reason why you got no reads counted is because chromosome names do not match between your annotation and your SAM file, you can check a few mapped reads in the SAM file to see if their chromosome names match those in your annotation. To compare the full list of chromosome names, you can compare the chr names included in the reference genome (your reads were mapped to) and chr names in your annotation to see if they match.

The screen usage provides format information for the '-A' option:

"  -A <string>         Provide a chromosome name alias file to match chr names in
                      annotation with those in the reads. This should be a two-
                      column comma-delimited text file. Its first column should
                      include chr names in the annotation and its second column
                      should include chr names in the reads. Chr names are case
                      sensitive. No column header should be included in the
                      file."

Also, you count your reads to miRNAs. Is this what you intended to do?

Best wishes,

Wei

messages.body_plain:
Your sam files includes mapping coordinates of reads in miRNA gene sequences whereas your GTF annotation includes coordinates of features in the whole genome. These are two completely different coordinate systems and they cannot work together.

You will have to map your reads to the genome and then use your current GTF file to get read counts, or try to obtain a GTF file in which the first column is miRNA gene names and then use your current bam files to count again this GTF file.

messages.subject_clean: [Bug] The Report Option "-R" Crashes featureCounts
messages.body_plain:
First, I found a bug in Samtools 1.2 (and presumably also in 1.0 and 1.1) in decoding type "B" extra tags (ie, the array-type tags). If the element type in the array is int8 or u_int8, and if the array tag is the last tag in the SAM line, Samtools will wrongly decide that the last element in the array breaks the memory boundary, thus it reports an error message and quits. I have built another BAM file that has the correct format, but Samtools 1.2 reported an error message on it. Your BAM file has a correct format.

I then found the bug in featureCounts that led to the error. The last block in your BAM file had only one read. FeatureCounts used a wrong variable to decide the block length, hence it tried to find the second read in the block. This made it running over the memory boundary. By fixing this bug, featueCounts worked properly on your BAM file. The next release should have this bug fixed; before that, you may sort your BAM file by using Samtools (no matter on coordinates or read names) before running featureCounts on it.

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I really like featureCounts so far, it's very fast (in most situtations) and easy to use. Thanks!

However, I'm experiencing some issues with a very large annotation file. I'm mapping reads to a large gene catalog (more than 11 million genes) and I have a simple GTF annotation file for the catalog that annotates each reference sequence across its whole length with a "gene_id" attribute. The complete GTF file is 996 MB in size, and contains annotations for 11,659,115 individual gene sequences. I realize this might not be the intended use-case for featureCounts, but I really like it and would love to use it for this as well.

Running featureCounts using only a small subset of the annotation file works well. I first tried with a subset containing only the first 50k annotations, then 100k, and at 250k it started to run fairly slowly, but when I tried with an annotation file containing 500k of the lines from the full file featureCounts really chokes. It sits forever (I got tired of waiting after an hour or so). I have an idea of what could be causing the issue; maybe it's due to the disparity between the number of reference sequences (what you call Features) and different "gene_id" variants (what you call Meta-features). There are only 7252 different meta-features in the full annotation file.

Here's the output from featureCounts when I try to run using the whole annotation file:

My guess is that it is stuck here doing lots of string concatenations for the output lines of each meta-feature, which would contain many many thousands of reference sequence headers due to the low ratio between meta-features and features. Do you think this might be the cause?
Would it be possible to skip outputting that information somehow, because I only need the summarized read counts, not so much all the other information (i.e. I would be happy with just columns 1 and 7-onwards of the output file).
